question.prompt: The minimum value of \(\sin\frac A2-\sqrt3\cos\frac A2\) is attained when \(A\) is

solutions.explanation:
No interval for \(A\) is specified, so minimize over all real angles measured in degrees. The coefficients \(1\) and \(\sqrt3\) suggest the special-angle values for \(60^\circ\). The sine subtraction identity gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin\frac A2-\sqrt3\cos\frac A2
&=2\left(\sin\frac A2\cos60^\circ
-\cos\frac A2\sin60^\circ\right)\\
&=2\sin\left(\frac A2-60^\circ\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since sine has minimum \(-1\), this expression has minimum \(-2\). It is attained exactly when
\[
\frac A2-60^\circ=-90^\circ+360^\circ k,
\]
where \(k\) is an integer. Thus
\[
A=-60^\circ+720^\circ k.
\]
None of the four listed angles has this form, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Rewrite as a shifted sine

solutions.explanation:
Take \(A\) over all real angles in degrees, since no interval is specified. Put \(t=A/2\), \(s=\sin t\), and \(c=\cos t\). The identity \(s^2+c^2=1\) lets us build a nonnegative expression containing the quantity we want to minimize:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(s+\frac12\right)^2
+\left(c-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2
&=s^2+c^2+s-\sqrt3c+1\\
&=2+s-\sqrt3c.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, \(s-\sqrt3c\ge-2\). Equality holds exactly when both squares vanish, giving
\[
\sin t=-\frac12,
\qquad
\cos t=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
On the unit circle, these values occur exactly at \(t=-30^\circ+360^\circ k\), where \(k\) is an integer. Hence the minimum \(-2\) occurs at
\[
A=-60^\circ+720^\circ k.
\]
None of the listed angles qualifies, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
